recipes.title: Chicken pho, light
recipes.summary: A clear, deeply spiced broth with poached chicken breast, a modest nest of rice noodles and a mountain of fresh herbs and sprouts.

steps.instruction: Halve the onion and ginger and char the cut sides in a dry pan over high heat until blackened in patches, about 6 minutes. This is not optional — the charring is where pho gets its depth.
Toast the star anise and cinnamon in the same pan for a minute until fragrant.
Add the chicken stock, charred aromatics and toasted spices to a large pot and bring to a bare simmer.
Lower the chicken breast into the broth and poach gently until cooked through, about 15 minutes. Lift it out, let it cool enough to handle, and shred it.
Leave the broth to infuse at the barest simmer while you prepare everything else. It should taste clean and aromatic, not cloudy.
Soak or boil the rice noodles according to the packet until just tender, then drain.
Strain the broth, discarding the aromatics, and season it with the fish sauce. Taste — it should be savoury and rounded.
Divide the noodles and shredded chicken breast between bowls, ladle over the hot broth, and top with bean sprouts, spring onions and cilantro. Serve with lime wedges.

recipes.storageNotes: Store the broth separately from the noodles or they turn to mush. Broth keeps three days refrigerated and freezes well for three months.

recipes.title: Chicken pho
recipes.summary: Charred ginger and onion, star anise and cinnamon simmered into a clear chicken broth, poured over rice noodles and shredded chicken.

steps.instruction: Halve the onion and ginger and char the cut sides in a dry pan over high heat until well blackened, about 7 minutes. The colour goes into the broth.
Toast the star anise and cinnamon in the same pan for a minute until you can smell them.
Combine the chicken stock, charred aromatics and spices in a large pot and bring to a bare simmer.
Poach the chicken breast in the broth until cooked through, about 16 minutes, then lift out and shred.
Leave the broth to infuse at the barest simmer. Never let it boil hard — a rolling boil turns a clear pho broth cloudy and it will not come back.
Soak or boil the rice noodles until just tender, then drain.
Strain the broth and season with the fish sauce.
Divide noodles and shredded chicken breast between bowls, ladle over the broth, and pile on bean sprouts, spring onions and cilantro. Serve with lime wedges.

recipes.storageNotes: Keep broth, noodles and toppings separate. The broth keeps three days refrigerated and freezes for three months; assemble fresh.

recipes.title: Chicken pho, hearty
recipes.summary: A big bowl of pho with extra chicken, a full nest of noodles and a soft egg, built for a proper appetite.

steps.instruction: Char the halved onion and ginger cut-side down in a dry pan over high heat until blackened, about 7 minutes.
Toast the star anise and cinnamon in the same pan for a minute.
Bring the chicken stock, charred aromatics and spices to a bare simmer in a large pot.
Poach the chicken breast in the broth until cooked through, about 18 minutes, then lift out and shred.
Boil the eggs for 7 minutes for a jammy yolk, cool under cold water and peel.
Leave the broth to infuse at the barest simmer, never letting it boil hard.
Soak or boil the rice noodles until just tender, then drain.
Strain the broth and season with the fish sauce.
Divide noodles and shredded chicken breast between bowls, ladle over the broth, and add halved eggs, bean sprouts, spring onions and cilantro. Serve with lime wedges.

recipes.storageNotes: Store broth, noodles and toppings separately. Broth keeps three days refrigerated and freezes for three months.

recipes.title: Ratatouille with white beans, light
recipes.summary: Slow-cooked summer vegetables in olive oil and thyme with white beans stirred through, using a restrained hand with the oil.

steps.instruction: Cut the aubergine into generous chunks, the courgette into half-moons and the bell pepper into strips. Keep the pieces large — small dice collapses into mush over a long cook.
Warm the olive oil in a wide heavy pan and cook the aubergine over medium-high heat until golden at the edges, about 8 minutes. It drinks oil, so resist adding more.
Add the onion and bell pepper and cook until softened, about 8 minutes, then stir in the garlic and thyme for a final minute.
Add the courgette and tinned tomatoes, season well, and bring to a gentle simmer.
Cook uncovered at a lazy simmer until the vegetables are completely tender and the tomatoes have reduced to a thick sauce that no longer pools.
Stir in the white beans and warm through for a few minutes. Taste and season again — it usually needs more salt than you expect.

recipes.storageNotes: Improves overnight and is good hot or at room temperature. Keeps four days refrigerated and freezes for three months.

recipes.title: Ratatouille with white beans
recipes.summary: Aubergine, courgette and peppers cooked down slowly in good olive oil with thyme and garlic, finished with white beans.

steps.instruction: Cut the aubergine into chunks, the courgette into half-moons and the bell pepper into strips, keeping every piece generous.
Warm two thirds of the olive oil in a wide heavy pan and brown the aubergine over medium-high heat until golden and yielding, about 8 minutes.
Add the onion and bell pepper and cook until soft and sweet, about 8 minutes. Stir in the garlic and thyme for the last minute, until fragrant but not coloured.
Add the courgette and tinned tomatoes, season generously, and bring to a gentle simmer.
Cook uncovered at a lazy simmer until everything is meltingly tender and the sauce is thick rather than watery.
Stir through the white beans and the remaining olive oil, warm for a few minutes, and season again to taste.

recipes.storageNotes: Better the next day, and good hot, warm or at room temperature. Keeps four days refrigerated and freezes for three months.

recipes.title: Ratatouille with white beans, hearty
recipes.summary: A fuller pan of ratatouille with extra beans and a generous pour of olive oil, substantial enough to be dinner on its own.

steps.instruction: Cut the aubergine into chunks, the courgette into half-moons and the bell pepper into strips.
Warm two thirds of the olive oil in a wide heavy pan and brown the aubergine until deeply golden, about 9 minutes.
Add the onion and bell pepper and cook until soft, about 9 minutes, stirring in the garlic and thyme at the end.
Add the courgette and tinned tomatoes, season well, and bring to a gentle simmer.
Simmer uncovered until the vegetables are completely tender and the sauce has thickened.
Stir in the white beans and the remaining olive oil and warm through. Season generously to finish.

recipes.storageNotes: Keeps four days refrigerated and improves overnight. Freezes for three months. Good hot or at room temperature.

recipes.title: Peanut butter and banana porridge, light
recipes.summary: Creamy oats cooked with milk, sweetened only by banana, with a spoon of peanut butter swirled through.

steps.instruction: Slice the banana, setting half aside for the top.
Put the rolled oats and whole milk in a pan with a pinch of salt and bring to a gentle simmer, stirring. The salt is not optional — porridge without it tastes flat however much fruit you add.
Cook, stirring often, until thick and creamy and the oats have lost their raw chalkiness, about 5 minutes. Mash in half the banana as it cooks.
Spoon into bowls, swirl through the peanut butter, and top with the reserved banana and the cinnamon.

recipes.storageNotes: Best eaten immediately. Leftovers thicken solid in the fridge; loosen with milk and reheat gently. Keeps two days.

recipes.title: Peanut butter and banana porridge
recipes.summary: Thick, creamy oats with banana cooked into them and a proper spoonful of peanut butter melting on top.

steps.instruction: Slice the banana, keeping half back for the top.
Combine the rolled oats and whole milk in a pan with a good pinch of salt and bring to a gentle simmer, stirring.
Cook, stirring regularly, until thick and creamy, about 5 minutes, mashing in half the banana towards the end. If it stiffens too far, loosen with a splash more milk.
Spoon into bowls, add the peanut butter so it melts into the surface, and finish with the reserved banana and the cinnamon.

recipes.storageNotes: Best fresh. Refrigerated it sets firm; reheat with extra milk. Keeps two days.

recipes.title: Peanut butter and banana porridge, hearty
recipes.summary: A big bowl of oats with plenty of peanut butter, a whole banana and a scatter of seeds for a breakfast that lasts until lunch.

steps.instruction: Slice the bananas, keeping half back for the top.
Toast the sesame seeds in a dry pan for a minute until fragrant, then tip out.
Combine the rolled oats and whole milk in the pan with a good pinch of salt and bring to a gentle simmer.
Cook, stirring, until thick and creamy, about 5 minutes, mashing in half the banana as it goes.
Spoon into bowls, add the peanut butter, and top with the reserved banana, the toasted sesame seeds and the cinnamon.

recipes.storageNotes: Best fresh. Keeps two days refrigerated; loosen with milk when reheating. Add the seeds after reheating so they stay crisp.

recipes.title: Turkish eggs, light
recipes.summary: Poached eggs over garlicky yoghurt with paprika butter and dill, with a wedge of bread for mopping.

steps.instruction: Stir the crushed garlic and a pinch of salt through the greek yogurt and leave it at room temperature. Cold yoghurt straight from the fridge will chill the eggs on contact.
Chop the dill weed and set aside. Toast the bread.
Bring a wide pan of water to a bare simmer, swirl it, and poach the eggs for about 3 minutes until the whites are set and the yolks still soft.
Melt the butter in a small pan with the paprika until it foams and turns deep orange, about a minute. Watch it — paprika burns fast and turns bitter.
Spread the yoghurt across two plates, set the drained eggs on top, spoon over the paprika butter and scatter with dill weed. Serve with the toast.

recipes.storageNotes: Assemble and eat immediately — poached eggs do not keep. The garlic yoghurt can be made a day ahead and refrigerated.

recipes.title: Turkish eggs
recipes.summary: Soft poached eggs on a bed of garlicky yoghurt, flooded with foaming paprika butter and finished with dill.

steps.instruction: Stir the crushed garlic and a good pinch of salt into the greek yogurt and leave it out to come to room temperature.
Chop the dill weed. Toast the bread.
Bring a wide pan of water to a bare simmer and poach the eggs for about 3 minutes, until the whites are just set and the yolks still liquid.
Melt the butter with the paprika in a small pan until foaming and deep orange, about a minute. Take it off the heat the moment it smells nutty.
Spread the yoghurt over two plates, set the drained eggs on top, pour over the paprika butter and scatter with dill weed. Serve with the toast.

recipes.storageNotes: Eat immediately — this does not keep once assembled. The garlic yoghurt can be made a day ahead.

recipes.title: Turkish eggs, hearty
recipes.summary: Six eggs over a deep bed of garlic yoghurt with plenty of paprika butter, dill and bread — a full weekend breakfast.

steps.instruction: Stir the crushed garlic and salt into the greek yogurt and let it sit at room temperature.
Chop the dill weed. Toast the bread.
Bring a wide pan of water to a bare simmer and poach the eggs in two batches, about 3 minutes each, so they do not crowd.
Melt the butter with the paprika until foaming and deep orange, about a minute.
Spread the yoghurt across two plates, pile on the drained eggs, pour over the paprika butter and scatter with dill weed. Serve with the toast.

recipes.storageNotes: Eat straight away. The garlic yoghurt keeps a day refrigerated; poach the eggs fresh.

recipes.title: Leek and potato soup, light
recipes.summary: Sweet softened leeks and potato blended into a smooth, comforting soup, kept light with stock rather than cream.

steps.instruction: Slice the leek and wash it thoroughly in a bowl of cold water — grit hides between the layers and will not come out later. Peel and dice the potato.
Melt the butter in a large pan and cook the leek gently with a pinch of salt until completely soft and sweet but not coloured, about 12 minutes. Browning them makes the soup taste harsh.
Add the potato, thyme and vegetable broth, bring to a simmer and cook until the potato falls apart at the press of a spoon.
Remove the thyme sprigs and blend until completely smooth.

recipes.storageNotes: Keeps four days refrigerated and freezes for three months. Reheat gently and stir well, as it separates a little on standing.

recipes.title: Leek and potato soup
recipes.summary: The classic: leeks softened in butter with floury potato, blended smooth and enriched with a little milk.

steps.instruction: Slice the leek and wash it well in cold water to get the grit out from between the layers. Peel and dice the potato.
Melt the butter in a large pan and sweat the leek with a pinch of salt until soft and sweet without taking on colour, about 13 minutes.
Add the potato, thyme and vegetable broth and simmer until the potato collapses easily under a spoon.
Fish out the thyme, blend until velvety, then stir in the whole milk and season well.

recipes.storageNotes: Keeps four days refrigerated and freezes for three months. Reheat gently without boiling once the milk is in.

recipes.title: Leek and potato soup, hearty
recipes.summary: A thicker, richer version with more potato and butter and a swirl of cream, served with bread to make a full meal.

steps.instruction: Slice and wash the leek thoroughly. Peel and dice the potato.
Melt the butter in a large pan and sweat the leek with salt until completely soft and sweet, about 14 minutes, without letting it colour.
Add the potato, thyme and vegetable broth and simmer until the potato is falling apart.
Remove the thyme and blend smooth, then stir in the whole milk and heavy cream and season generously.
Toast the bread and serve alongside.

recipes.storageNotes: Keeps three days refrigerated. Reheat gently and never boil once the cream is in. Freeze before adding the dairy for best results.
